t: Maximize Value of Function in a Ball Passing Game — Binary Lifting
o: From a start i, the ball follows receiver[i], receiver[receiver[i]], ... for k passes; the score sums every touched index including the start. k can be 1e10 and n is 1e5, so simulating pass-by-pass (O(nk)) is impossible. Functional graphs + huge step counts call for binary lifting: precompute up[j][i] = destination after 2^j passes and sm[j][i] = sum of the 2^j receivers visited (indices receiver[..], excluding the sender i itself). Decompose k into powers of two and accumulate. For [2,0,1], k=4, starting at 2: path 2,1,0,2,1 sums to 6, matching the expected output.
k: k up to 1e10 demands O(log k) stepping — binary lifting on the functional graph.
Score for start i = i + sum of receiver-indices over k hops, accumulated power-of-two by power-of-two.

a.i: Directly follow the ball for k passes from each start. Correct and simple, but O(nk) — up to 1e15 operations — so it only serves to validate the fast solution on small inputs.
s: For each start i, set cur = i, total = i.
Repeat k times: cur = receiver[cur]; total += cur.
a.t: O(n*k) — quadratic in the wrong dimension; only viable for tiny k.

a.i: Build B = bit_length(k) levels of jump tables. Level 0 stores one hop (destination and received-index sum). Higher levels compose two half-jumps. Answering a query is decomposing k in binary: for each set bit j, add sm[j][cur] to the total and move cur = up[j][cur]. Total score adds the starting index i separately.
s: Let B = number of bits in k. Set up[0] = receiver, sm[0] = receiver.
For j in 1..B-1, fill up[j][i] = up[j-1][up[j-1][i]] and sm[j][i] = sm[j-1][i] + sm[j-1][up[j-1][i]].
For each start i: cur = i, tot = i; for each set bit j of k: tot += sm[j][cur], cur = up[j][cur].

c.python:
class Solution:
    def getMaxFunctionValue(self, receiver: List[int], k: int) -> int:
        n = len(receiver)
        B = k.bit_length()
        up = [receiver[:]]
        sm = [receiver[:]]
        for j in range(1, B):
            pu, ps = up[j - 1], sm[j - 1]
            up.append([pu[pu[i]] for i in range(n)])
            sm.append([ps[i] + ps[pu[i]] for i in range(n)])
        ans = 0
        for i in range(n):
            cur, tot, j = i, i, 0
            kk = k
            while kk:
                if kk & 1:
                    tot += sm[j][cur]
                    cur = up[j][cur]
                kk >>= 1
                j += 1
            ans = max(ans, tot)
        return ans

a.t: O(n log k) — table construction dominates; each of the n starts then walks O(log k) bits.
a.sp: O(n log k) — roughly 34 levels of two n-sized tables.

w: Binary lifting is the standard answer whenever a functional graph must be traversed an astronomically large number of steps. Pitfalls: the score includes the starting index i (add it upfront), the sum tables exclude senders (only receivers are summed), and JavaScript needs BigInt for k up to 1e10 combined with n-term sums. Follow-ups: answer many (start, k) queries offline, or find the start maximizing the score after exactly k passes where scores use node weights.
